title: Shoyu Ramen
subtitle: Japanese soy-sauce ramen with a clear, savoury broth
excerpt: Shoyu ramen is the Tokyo style: a clear, amber-coloured broth seasoned with soy sauce, served over springy egg noodles with a soft-boiled egg and spring onion. The broth is simple to make and far better than anything from a packet.
sourceNotes: Shoyu ramen originates in Tokyo and uses a clear chicken or pork broth seasoned with soy sauce. It is one of the four main regional ramen styles in Japan.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the broth in portions for up to 3 months. Do not freeze noodles or boiled eggs.
recipe.batchNotes: Make a large batch of broth and freeze in portions for quick ramen any night.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth can be made up to 3 days ahead and refrigerated. Cook eggs and noodles fresh before serving.

content.text: Shoyu ramen is built around the tare: the seasoning concentrate that is added to the broth just before serving rather than cooked in from the start. Here, a mixture of light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and mirin forms the tare. Kept separate until serving, it gives you precise control over the saltiness of each bowl.

The broth itself is infused with ginger, garlic and a small amount of sake, then finished with sesame oil. Simmering for 25 to 30 minutes is enough to extract good flavour from the aromatics without the broth going cloudy.
Nori (dried seaweed sheets) is a classic ramen topping: add a sheet per bowl just before serving. Bamboo shoots and a slice of chashu pork are other traditional garnishes.
Make the tare: combine the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce and mirin in a small bowl. Set aside.

Pour the chicken stock into the large saucepan. Add the ginger, garlic and sake. Bring to a gentle simmer over a medium heat and cook for 25 minutes. Do not boil vigorously or the broth will turn cloudy. Remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil. Strain through a fine sieve and discard the aromatics. Keep the broth warm over a low heat.

Cook the soft-boiled eggs: bring a small pan of water to a rolling boil. Lower the eggs in gently and cook for exactly 6 minutes and 30 seconds. Transfer immediately to a bowl of cold water and leave for at least 5 minutes before peeling. The yolk should be jammy and slightly soft at the centre.
Cook the noodles according to the packet instructions. Drain and divide between two deep warmed bowls.
Add half the tare to each bowl (about 30ml per bowl). Pour the hot broth over the noodles, stirring briefly to combine the tare. Taste and add a little more tare if the broth needs more salt.
Halve the soft-boiled eggs lengthways and place one on top of each bowl. Scatter over the spring onion and serve immediately.

items.cause: The stock was boiled too hard or for too long.
items.fix: Keep the heat at a gentle simmer throughout. If the broth has already gone cloudy, strain it through a fine sieve lined with a piece of kitchen paper, which will pull out some of the particles.

items.symptom: The broth tastes flat or thin
items.cause: The base stock was low-quality or the aromatics did not infuse long enough.
items.fix: Add a little more tare (soy mixture) a teaspoon at a time and taste after each addition. A splash of fish sauce can also deepen the savouriness without making it taste Japanese-fusion.

items.symptom: The egg yolk is fully set
items.cause: The egg cooked for too long or the water was not at a full boil when it went in.
items.fix: Use 6 minutes 30 seconds in a properly boiling pan for a jammy yolk. Fridge-cold eggs may need an extra 30 seconds. Always transfer to cold water immediately after cooking.

items.cause: They were left to sit after draining.
items.fix: Divide and bowl the noodles immediately after draining. If they have stuck, run briefly under hot water to loosen before serving.
